memo: Base: the pipeline embedded in sanpier's 'Candidate-aware PubChem promotion 0.465' (frozen_0465 = dmitriigluzdov 'CASMI 26: The Data Behind Spectra to Structures' v16 + sanpier's rank-1 PubChem promotion), kernels/e3/base_f465.ipynb, + ours own COCONUT + lfrag (e3f465oc-1, LB 0.467, our best). New part (ours, 10-26): fold-safe FPNet ensemble. dmitriigluzdov/casmi26-fold-safe-fpnet holds 5 FPNets, each trained without one identity-disjoint fold (68% top-1 on never-seen molecules vs 97% seen); the base uses fold0 alone in the PubChem channel and full1 alone in the engine. fpe=1 (this version): PubChem channel logits = A, B (1/3 each) + mean of the 5 fold models (1/3); ebe=1: engine FP bank = full1 (1/2) + mean of the 5 fold models (1/2). Why: the 10-25 ON/OFF square (neural rerank 0.467, two-pipeline fusion 0.466, both 0.466) showed the overlay is saturated (also cosmorin's gap analysis: rank 1 is 0.504, the gap is upstream in the spectrum model); the neural rerank at offset 1-3 can never change rank 1, while the FPNet decides rank 1 for library-less molecules (hidden test = never-seen Enveda NPs, where FPNet top-1 is 42% unseen vs 89% seen). Averaging independently trained models lowers prediction variance on unseen spectra. Hypothesis: LB >= 0.470. Effect size: the PubChem channel enters the final list through the gate / promotion for library-weak molecules; top-1 changes expected in 2-3% of molecules (8-12 of 400). This version is the split of the bundle e3f465fe-1 (fpe + ebe): fpe only (the engine keeps full1 alone, so its ranker sees the same feature scale it was trained on). With e3f465oc-1 (neither) and e3f465fe-1 (both) it reads which half moves. build.py f465fp base=f465 ownco=1 lfrag=1 fpe=1.
message: e3f465fp-1: f465 + own COCONUT + lfrag (0.467) + our fold-safe FPNet ensemble in the PubChem channel only
